Action Plan:
1. Prescribed a 3-day course of oral antibiotics (twice daily; drug / dose / route not documented) for presumed urinary tract infection; electronic prescription sent to the patient’s nominated pharmacy.  
2. Instructed patient to begin antibiotics immediately upon collection.  
3. Safety-net advice: if abdominal pain worsens, temperature rises, back pain develops, or any new/recurrent urinary symptoms occur, patient to seek urgent review and may require face-to-face assessment.  
4. No additional concerns raised; patient voiced understanding and had no further questions.  
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: 2-day history of lower abdominal (mid-line) pain.  
• Associated symptoms: mild nausea (no vomiting), subjective sweating, slight pink discoloration of urine, mild increase in urinary frequency, no dysuria, no back pain, no foul urine odor.  
• Gastrointestinal: constipation last week, now resolved; normal bowel motion 2 h ago; no blood in stool.  
• Gynecological: regular periods; no inter-menstrual or post-coital bleeding; no vaginal discharge.  
• System review: no upper abdominal pain, no heartburn, no recent travel.  
• Past medical history: no chronic illnesses reported.  
• Surgical history: none reported.  
• Allergies: amoxicillin.  
• Medications: none regular; no OTC; contraceptive implant removed 1 yr ago.  
• Family history: mother – treated early-stage breast cancer.  
• Social: lives with parents; alcohol—≈1 beer on 4 days/week; non-smoker.

Objective:
• Self-recorded temperature 37 °C one hour prior to consultation.  
• No other vital signs or physical examination documented.  
• No investigations performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Lower abdominal pain / possible urinary tract infection  
   - Assessment: Suspected uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis).  
   - Differential diagnosis: pelvic inflammatory disease, early appendicitis, gastrointestinal causes (resolved constipation).  
   - Investigations planned: none at this time; advise re-evaluation if symptoms escalate.  
   - Treatment planned: 3-day course of oral antibiotics twice daily (drug/dose/route not documented) with avoidance of amoxicillin due to allergy.  
   - Referrals: arrange face-to-face GP review or urgent care if deterioration or red-flag symptoms arise.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected: documented abdominal and pelvic examination, urinalysis, pregnancy test, full vital signs, antibiotic name/dose/route, detailed allergy reaction description.  
● Internal conflicts: none noted.  
● Transcript quality: generally clear; occasional inaudible words but did not affect extraction of key clinical information.
